newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: M&R warns year profits to fall.
newsitem.headline: M&R warns year profits to fall.

text.p: South Africa's Murray & Roberts Ltd said on Thursday that its headline and total earnings for the full year to June 30, 1997, would be lower than the comparable period last year.
The firm earlier posted first half headline earnings per share of 18 cents -- a drop of 65 percent over last time.
The firm said the drop in year profits would be due to a substantial increase in its interest charge for the full year.

It added that, although it would receive a second half boost from the sale of its Fedstone unit, the level of non-operating profit in the period was unlikely to be as big as that seen in the first half.
The firm has been dogged by provisions related to several major contracts, especially the supply of carriages to a new rapid transit system in Taiwan called Dorts.

M&R said the trains deal was still a problem. "The major train contracts remain the main area of concern. Strenuous efforts to achieve an early settlement of the Dorts dispute and the related insurance claims continue," the firm said.
The problem relates to the supply of carriages to Germany's Siemens which then failed certain stress tests.
"A mediation process is underway to prevent a costly proces of arbitration," the firm said.

The group said other problems included a further provision on its Intershore oil rig joint-venture contract for the supply and hook up of two oil platforms in Angola and a fire at the Alloy Wheels International (AWI) plant in Britain.
A new AWI plant in Port Elizabeth also had a slower than expected start-up.
The firm said its materials unit performed well despite difficult markets and its transport unit also posted healthy profits.
